newsitem.title: GUAM: Korean Air faces angry relatives at briefing.
newsitem.headline: Korean Air faces angry relatives at briefing.

text.p: Korean Air Lines officials faced an angry barrage of criticism from relatives of passengers aboard its crashed jumbo jet at a news conference on Wednesday.
The news conference erupted in shouts from about 30 relatives of passengers saying that KAL had not released the names of survivors of the crash.
The officials offered little new information at the news conference at a hotel in Agana, Guam's capital, repeating that they believed about 30 passengers had survived the overnight crash.

They also said that the flight data and voice recorders from the Boeing 747 had been sent for analysis and that they would not comment on possible causes of the crash before the analysis was complete.
The officials said a special KAL flight from Seoul, South Korea, would bring another 200 relatives of the passengers to Guam.
The jetliner was carrying 231 passengers, mainly holidaymakers, and 23 crew. It crashed overnight into a hilly jungle area near Guam's main international airport.
